editorial:
Ever feel like you just need to throw your phone in a lake and run away from the city? That is exactly what the couple in this movie does. They leave the noise of Brooklyn for a quiet house upstate to fix their relationship and get some peace. The vibe is light and funny at first, focusing on how hard it is for modern people to exist without scrolling through social media every five seconds. You will probably find yourself laughing at their struggle to actually talk to each other without a screen in the way, making the whole setup feel very relatable.

What makes this flick work is the irony of their situation. While they are finally bonding, they have no idea that aliens are wiping out humanity. The acting is natural, and the pacing keeps you guessing about when they will finally realize the world is ending. It is a great pick if you want something that mixes laughs with a bit of sci-fi chaos. You can rent it on Apple TV or stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best experience. If you love quirky indie films, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a smart move.
endingExplained: The couple eventually discovers that the rest of the world has been taken over by aliens while they were offline. They find out they are some of the last humans left. In a funny twist, their choice to disconnect actually saved them from the initial attack. They end up having to navigate a ruined world, realizing that while phones are distracting, they are pretty useful when you need to know if monsters are attacking your town.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark comedies about the end of the world.
